title: Assert-based unit test (Python)
description: The simplest real test: call the function and assert the result. No framework needed — a failing assert raises and fails loudly. Worked example: run add cases mentally — inputs bind as written, each step follows the code path described below, and the final value is PASS.
code:
def add(a, b):
    return a + b

assert add(2, 3) == 5
assert add(-1, 1) == 0
print("PASS")
how_it_works: Each assert evaluates the call and compares; the first failure raises AssertionError with the line number.

test_cases.note: Determinism check: re-running the snippet reproduces the identical output.

pitfalls: Bare asserts vanish under python -O — frameworks keep them always-on.
